note: FROZEN gold calibration set. Never used in training. hard = speak/wait graded strictly; unsure = boundary cases, excluded from hard accuracy, model should sit near threshold there.
policy_notes: Policy carried over from my production voice stack (learned on a real 8 kHz phone line): Never interrupt a data readout (numbers, spellings, addresses), the pause between digits can run long and the agent still waits. A bare acknowledgement ("thanks", "okay got it") is a complete turn, speak, but turn-complete never means call-over; on telephony audio "thanks" and "next" collide and a misheard "thanks" once ended a live call, so ending is a separate explicit decision. When the caller asks for time ("hang on, let me check"), patience extends well past the normal window, then check in gently instead of answering. Hedges are usually handoffs, "I guess that's all" means it's my turn; respond and let barge-in recovery cover the miss. A complete statement that answers my question gets an immediate response; one that opens a new topic gets a beat of grace. Self-interrupts ("book me on the- wait") get extended patience, a new thought is coming. Where costs are asymmetric, prefer absolute rules over conditional ones; every conditional version of my hang-up rule measured worse in production than the absolute one.
